Busy-waiting repeatedly checks a status flag in a CPU loop. …

qs.stem: Microprocessor memory and other parts of the microcomputer are physically connected through which of the following ?
qs.sol: The paper identifies the address bus as the physical bus linking a processor with memory and other system components for selecting locations. A complete system also uses data and control buses.

qs.stem: Microprocessor memory and other parts of the microcomputer are physically connected through which of the following ?
qs.sol:
These are the four main memory access methods used in computer systems:
 Sequential Access – Memory is accessed in a linear sequence.

Direct Access – Data is accessed by moving directly to a general location and then sequentially to the exact spot.

Random Access – Any memory location can be accessed directly (e.g., RAM).

Associative Access – A special form of random access where data is accessed based on content rather than address.

qs.stem: The main virtue for using single Bus structure is

opts.C: cost effective connectivity and ease of attaching peripheral devices
opts.D:
cheaper in price

E

Question not attempted

qs.sol:
CONCEPT: A single-bus structure connects the processor, main memory and all I/O devices to one common set of shared wires (the system bus). The defining trade-off of this design is simplicity and economy versus throughput: because every transfer shares the same path, the structure is cheap and uniform to build, but only one device pair can use the bus at any instant.

Two consequences follow directly from this single shared path:

Economy of wiring: a single set of address, data and control lines serves the whole machine, so far less cabling/interconnect is needed than in a multi-bus design — this keeps cost low. …

qs.stem: In a microcomputer system, what does the address bus facilitate?
qs.sol:
Answer:  ARM stands for Advanced RISC Machine.
 ARM processors are high-speed, low-power chips with small die sizes. They are widely used in PDAs, handheld devices, mobile phones, games, and many consumer products because of their efficient RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) architecture.
 Key points:
 Small die size and low power consumption.

qs.stem: In memory mapped I/O

opts.A: the I/O devices and the memory share the same address space
opts.B: the I/O devices have a separate address space
opts.C: the memory and I/O devices have an associated address space
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
In memory-mapped I/O, peripheral registers occupy addresses in the ordinary memory address space.

The processor can access them with ordinary load and store instructions, unlike isolated port addressing.

qs.stem: In a microcomputer system, what does the address bus facilitate?

opts.A: Communication between the CPU and memory
opts.B: Communication between the CPU and input devices
opts.C: Communication between the CPU and output devices
opts.D: Communication between the memory and input devices

qs.sol:
The CPU places a memory address on the address bus to select a location.

The selected memory then participates in a read or write using the data and control buses.

Major requirements for an I/O module are:
 Processor communication

Control and timing

Data buffering

Device communication

Error detection

qs.stem: The ____ is a popular high-bandwidth, processor-independent bus that can function as a mezzanine or peripheral bus.
qs.sol: PCI (Peripheral Component Interconnect) is a widely used, high-bandwidth, processor-independent bus. It can operate as a mezzanine or peripheral bus and supports a wide range of microprocessor-based systems, including single- and multi-processor configurations.

qs.stem: What do we use to extend the connectivity of the processor bus?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
To extend the connectivity of the processor bus, a PCI (Peripheral Component Interconnect) bus is used.

Why PCI bus?

It acts as an expansion bus

Connects processor to:

Peripheral devices

I/O controllers

Provides high-speed communication

Helps overcome limitations of direct processor bus connections

Hence, PCI bus is used to extend processor bus connectivity

qs.stem: What is the primary role of the memory-mapped I/O technique in a microcontroller?

opts.A: It increases the speed of program execution
opts.B: It provides additional memory space for data storage
opts.C: It allows I/O registers to be accessed using memory addresses
opts.D: It eliminates the need for I/O operations

qs.sol: In memory-mapped I/O, peripheral or I/O control registers are assigned addresses in the processor’s memory address space. The CPU can then access those registers using ordinary memory read/write instructions. Thus, the primary role is to allow I/O registers to be accessed through memory addresses.

qs.stem: In a DMA-based system, the DMA controller transfers a word of data by temporarily taking control of the memory bus. This technique is known as:

opts.D:
Cycle Stealing

E

Question not attempted

qs.sol: In cycle stealing, the DMA controller briefly takes a memory-bus cycle from the CPU to transfer one word, then releases the bus. The CPU may be delayed for that cycle, but the controller need not monopolize the bus for an entire block.
Intel introduced the PCI (Peripheral Component Interconnect) bus in 1992 to standardize high-speed peripheral connections.

qs.stem:
State whether the following sentences are true or false.
 (i) With memory-mapped I/O, a single read line and a single write line are needed on the bus.
 (ii) With isolated I/O, the address space for I/O is isolated from that for memory.
qs.sol:
Concept

An address space is a logical set of addresses interpreted within a transaction type; it does not mean a separate bundle of physical address wires.

Memory-mapped I/O places device registers in the memory address space and uses memory-style read/write controls. Isolated I/O creates a separate port address space selected by I/O instructions or control signals.

Application

In memory-mapped I/O, memory and I/O transactions use the same read and write control paths, while an address decoder selects either memory or a device register. Therefore one read line and one write line can serve both. …

qs.stem: In various devices, ____ are used to overcome the difference in data transfer speed.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
To overcome differences in data transfer speed between devices, buffer registers are used. These registers temporarily store data when the receiving device is not ready, allowing the sender to continue without waiting. This helps synchronize data flow between devices operating at different speeds.
 Multiple buses increase data throughput but do not address speed mismatches. Speed-enhancing circuitries boost processing speed but do not manage data timing. Therefore, only buffer registers are specifically designed for this purpose.

qs.stem: The communication between the components in a microcomputer takes place via the address and _____.
qs.sol:
Answer:  The communication between components takes place via the address bus and the data bus.
 Address bus: carries address information used to select a memory location or an I/O device.

qs.stem: The communication between the components in a microcomputer takes place via the address and _____.
qs.sol: Intel introduced the first commercial microprocessor in 1971—the 4-bit Intel 4004. It is regarded as the first general-purpose microprocessor.

qs.stem: What is the signal used to interrupt processor and to execute service routine that takes an error recovery action?
qs.sol:
Concept

A processor can learn about an I/O event either by repeatedly checking device status or through an interrupt. A time-out is an exception event raised when an operation does not finish within a preset interval.

When that event is configured as an interrupt source, control transfers to a service routine, which can diagnose the stalled operation and initiate recovery.

Application

The stem asks for a signal that interrupts the processor specifically so that an error-recovery service routine can run. Among the offered values, Time-out denotes the expiry event associated with a stalled or overlong operation, so it fits that mechanism. …

qs.stem: What is the signal used to interrupt processor and to execute service routine that takes an error recovery action?
qs.sol: CD-ROM  stores data in a single continuous spiral groove (track) on the disc. A laser reads data sequentially along this spiral.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is true with reference to an interrupt occurred?

opts.A: CPU immediately jumps to a new process without completing the current instruction.
opts.B: CPU completes the execution of current instruction.
opts.C: CPU completes execution of all instructions in current process before jumping to a new process.

qs.sol: When a hardware interrupt occurs, the processor completes the instruction currently being executed before branching to the Interrupt Service Routine (ISR). This ensures system stability and data integrity. Therefore, the CPU does not abandon an instruction mid-execution.

qs.stem: A 50 kbps device is connected to a processor. The interrupt overhead is 50 μsec. The minimum performance achieved when interrupt is initiated and data transfer is used instead of programmed I/O is:
qs.sol:
Concept: For a rate R bits/s, an interrupt that services b bits has a transfer interval T = b / R. If the interrupt overhead is Ti, the relative performance factor is S = T / Ti = b / (R × Ti). Because b is a positive whole number of bits, the minimum possible factor occurs at the smallest transfer granularity, b = 1 bit.

Application:

Set R = 50 kbps = 50,000 bits per second and Ti = 50 μsec.

For the minimum, use b = 1 bit, so T = b / R = 1 / 50,000 second = 20 μsec.

Substitute into the factor: Smin = T / Ti = 20 μsec / 50 μsec = 0.4.

Cross-check: Equivalently, R × Ti = 50,000 × 50 × 10−6 = 2.5, so Smin = 1 / 2.5 = 0.4. …

qs.stem: A 50 kbps device is connected to a processor. The interrupt overhead is 50 μsec. The minimum performance achieved when interrupt is initiated and data transfer is used instead of programmed I/O is:
qs.sol:
Statement  (A) is correct  because assembly language uses  mnemonics  (like MOV, ADD) to represent operation codes.

Statement  (B) is incorrect  because writing assembly programs is  not easy or time-saving ; it is low-level and more complex.

Statement  (C) is incorrect  because assembly language is  machine dependent , not machine-independent.

Therefore,  only statement (A) is correct  → correct answer is  option (4) .

qs.stem: A device has been used in cycle stealing mode of DMA. A word of 4 bytes can be transferred when it is available. The memory cycle time is 40 ms and CPU is idle for 10% of its time. What is the data transfer rate of the device?
qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: the printed phrase “data transfer rate” is ambiguous about whether the stolen memory cycle is included. The final key credits 11.11 B/sec, treating the rate as the device producing a 4-byte word every 360 ms: 40/(360+40)=10% CPU idle and 4/0.360≈11.11 B/sec. Counting the complete 400 ms cycle instead gives 10 B/sec.

qs.stem: For which of the following is an interrupt mechanism NOT required?

opts.A: When programs request a system call to be performed by the operating system
opts.B: To give the user better control over the computer
opts.C: To allow the processes to manage shared data
opts.D: To handle mismatch between CPU and device speeds

qs.sol: Shared-data coordination uses synchronization primitives and atomicity; it does not inherently require an interrupt for each access.

topics.deep:
- **I/O interface:** an interface (I/O module) sits between CPU/bus and peripheral. Roles: **resolve differences in speed, data format and signal levels**, buffer data in internal registers, decode device address, provide status, and generate interrupts. I/O commands: **control** (activate peripheral, tell it what to do), **status** (test conditions), **data output** (bus to device), **data input** (interface responds by putting data from its register on the bus).
- **Addressing I/O:** **isolated (I/O-mapped)** uses separate IN/OUT instructions and a separate I/O address space; **memory-mapped** gives device registers memory addresses so ordinary LOAD/STORE work.
- **Three data-transfer modes:**

| Mode | Who starts/controls | CPU role | Speed/use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Programmed I/O | CPU, via instructions | **polls status register in a loop (busy-waiting)**, wastes cycles | slow, simple devices |
| Interrupt-driven I/O | device interrupts when ready | does other work, services ISR | medium; keyboard, mouse |
| DMA | DMA controller | only starts and ends the transfer | fastest; **disk, block transfers** |

- **Programmed I/O flow:** read status register; if ready flag set, read/write data register; repeat. The **status register** is checked, not the instruction or address register.
- **Interrupt processing:** device raises IRQ -> CPU finishes current instruction -> saves PC and flags (on stack) -> obtains ISR address (**vectored**: device supplies vector; **non-vectored**: fixed address) -> runs **ISR** -> restores context and returns. **Maskable** interrupts can be disabled, **non-maskable** (e.g. power failure, 8085 TRAP) cannot. **Software interrupts** (INT n, system call) vs hardware interrupts.
- **Priority interrupt:** a system that decides which of several simultaneous requests is serviced first. Methods: **polling** (software, slowest), **daisy chaining** (serial hardware priority; closest device has highest priority), **parallel priority** (interrupt mask register + priority encoder; fastest and flexible). Daisy chain also describes devices connected one after another (A to B to C to computer).
- **DMA:** DMA controller (registers: address, word count, control/status) takes over the buses. Handshake: controller asserts **Bus Request (BR)** -> CPU finishes the bus cycle and replies **Bus Grant (BG)** and puts its buses in high-impedance (tri-state) -> controller drives address and read/write lines and transfers -> releases the bus and may raise an interrupt on completion. When **BG = 1**, the read and write lines are **outputs** from the DMA controller (when BG = 0 they are inputs so CPU can program the DMA registers). Transfer modes: **burst (block) mode** - a whole block in one continuous sequence, CPU is locked out, **best for fast devices like magnetic disks**; **cycle stealing** - controller takes one bus cycle at a time, slows CPU slightly; **transparent** - uses bus only when CPU does not. DMA channel = resource letting a device transfer without loading CPU. **I/O processors (channels)** go further: selector channel (one fast device at a time), multiplexer channel (many slow devices).
- **System bus:** **data bus** (bidirectional, carries data between processor, memory, I/O; **width = number of lines** = word size, e.g. 32), **address bus** (unidirectional from CPU; width decides addressable memory 2^n), **control bus** (read/write, memory/IO select, interrupt request/acknowledge, bus request/grant, clock, reset; **controls access to and use of data and address lines**). A bus is a shared communication pathway connecting two or more devices. **Bandwidth = width x clock rate** (e.g. 64-bit at 100 MHz = 800 MB/s).
- **Bus timing and arbitration:** **synchronous** (common clock) vs **asynchronous** (handshake signals: request/acknowledge, strobe). Arbitration decides which master gets the bus: **daisy-chain, polling, independent request (parallel)**; centralised vs distributed. Time to coordinate is governed by signal **propagation delay**.
- **Standards:**

| Standard | Full form / note |
|---|---|
| SCSI | **Small Computer System Interface** - a bus supporting local disk drives and other peripherals |
| PCI | Peripheral Component Interconnect (parallel) |
| **PCIe** | PCI **Express** (serial point-to-point lanes) |
| USB | Universal Serial Bus - 1.1: 12 Mbps, 2.0: 480 Mbps, 3.0: 5 Gbps |
| SATA / PATA(IDE) | disk interfaces serial / parallel |
| IEEE 1394 | FireWire |
| RS-232 | serial port standard (printers, scanners, modems earlier) |
| HDMI / VGA | video output |

- **Serial vs parallel:** serial sends bits one by one on few wires, cheaper cabling, suitable for long distance, subclasses synchronous and asynchronous (start/stop bits); parallel sends several bits simultaneously on multiple lines, faster over short distances but suffers skew and crosstalk and needs bulky cables.
- **I/O buffer register:** holds data exchanged between CPU and I/O module (distinct from MAR which holds the address and MBR which holds memory data).
- **Likely question angles:** (1) compare programmed, interrupt and DMA on CPU involvement; (2) which transfer for a keyboard, printer or hard disk; (3) bus bandwidth calculation; (4) address bus width and memory size; (5) daisy-chain priority order; (6) maskable vs non-maskable interrupt example; (7) cycle stealing vs burst; (8) vectored vs non-vectored interrupt; (9) USB version speeds; (10) steps in DMA handshake and meaning of BR and BG; (11) synchronous vs asynchronous bus.

topics.title: 6. Computer Arithmetic, Floating Point & Micro-operations
topics.theory:
- **Sign bit:** **0 = positive, 1 = negative** (signed magnitude/2's complement MSB).
- **IEEE 754 floating point:** **single precision = 32 bits: 1 sign + 8 exponent (bias 127) + 23 mantissa/fraction**; **double precision = 64 bits: 1 + 11 exponent (bias 1023) + 52 mantissa**. Value = (−1)^s × 1.f × 2^(e−bias). 0 10000011 100101… → exponent 131−127 = 4 → 1.1001010 × 2⁴ = 11001.01₂ = 25.25.
- **Normalisation:** mantissa adjusted so the most significant digit is non-zero (1.xxx or 0.1xxx); (0.10101)₂ = 0.10101 × 2⁰ in normalised form. **Alignment** of exponents happens before add/subtract.
- **Booth's algorithm** multiplies signed binary numbers efficiently using recoding of the multiplier (pairs Qn, Qn+1: 10 → subtract multiplicand, 01 → add).
- **Micro-operations** (register transfer): **four types — register transfer, arithmetic, logic, shift**. `R3 ← R1 + R̅2 + 1` = R1 plus the 2's complement of R2 (**subtraction R1 − R2**). Logic micro-ops on 4-bit R1 = 1010, R2 = 1100: AND = 1000, OR = 1110, XOR = 0110.
- A control unit specifies the micro-operations to be executed (via control words in microprogram).

qs.stem: Number with decimal points is called _____ in programming language.
qs.sol:
In programming and computer representation, a number containing a decimal point is called a floating-point number.

Modified from the official paper: The printed phrase “Fractional point numbers” is not the standard term for numbers with decimal points; the bank uses “Floating point numbers”.
qs.rel: Floating point numbers carry a fractional part (stored as sign, exponent, mantissa); integers do not. Neighbours: float vs double precision, complex numbers in some languages, fixed-point representation.

qs.stem: The speed of supercomputer is measured in ____ .
qs.sol: Floating-point operations per second
qs.rel: Supercomputer performance is in FLOPS (floating-point operations per second): MFLOPS, GFLOPS, TFLOPS, PFLOPS. Mainframes/general computers are rated in MIPS. India's PARAM series are supercomputers.

qs.stem:
Which of the following pair regarding sign bit is correct?
 I. 0 – Positive
 II. 1 – Negative
qs.sol: Both I and II
qs.rel: Sign bit: 0 positive, 1 negative, in the MSB. In 2's complement the same convention holds with range -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1)-1; sign-magnitude has two zeros.

qs.stem: How many bits are there for exponent in IEEE 754 single precision floating point representation?
qs.sol: The IEEE 754 single precision floating-point standard uses a total of 32 bits. This structure is divided into three parts: one sign bit, eight exponent bits, and twenty-three mantissa bits. Therefore, the exponent field specifically requires 8 bits to represent the power of two.
qs.rel: IEEE 754 single: 1 sign + 8 exponent (bias 127) + 23 fraction = 32 bits. Double: 1 + 11 (bias 1023) + 52 = 64. Value = (-1)^s x 1.f x 2^(e-bias).

qs.stem: ‘PUSH A’ indicates which instruction format? Assume A denotes a fixed implicit accumulator register and is not encoded as an address field.
qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: the key ticks zero-address although “PUSH A” appears to name an explicit operand; A is now specified as an implicit, unencoded register.

Instruction address count is the number of address fields encoded in the instruction, not the number of registers involved in execution.

Under the stated assumption, PUSH uses A without any encoded address field, so the instruction has zero explicit addresses.
qs.rel: Address count is the number of address fields encoded in the instruction: PUSH/POP and stack ALU operations are zero-address, with operands implicit on stack top. One-address uses implied accumulator.

qs.stem:
This instruction is of what type?
 Instruction
 ADD R1, A, B
qs.sol:
To classify the instruction ADD R1, A, B, count the number of operands specified.

The instruction has three operands: R1 (destination), A (first source), and B (second source).

Instructions that specify three operands are known as three address instructions.

Therefore, this instruction is a three address instruction.
qs.rel: Count operands in the instruction: ADD R1,A,B has destination and two sources, so three-address. Two-address ADD A,B overwrites one source; one-address uses AC; zero-address uses stack.

qs.stem: In which of the following data transfer modes does the CPU constantly monitor the peripheral and stay in a program loop until the peripheral device becomes ready for data transfer?
qs.sol: The described mode is programmed I/O. The CPU continuously polls the peripheral status register and remains in a loop until the device becomes ready for data transfer.
qs.rel: Programmed I/O: CPU polls the device status in a program loop (busy-waiting) until the device is ready. Contrast interrupt-initiated I/O and DMA, where the CPU is free or uninvolved.

qs.stem: In which of the following processes, during floating point arithmetic operations is mantissa adjusted so that the most significant bit is nonzero?
qs.sol:
Floating-point normalisation shifts the mantissa and adjusts the exponent.

It places the leading significant bit in the required nonzero position.
qs.rel: Normalisation shifts the mantissa so its leading digit is non-zero, adjusting the exponent. Alignment (equalising exponents) is done before add/subtract. Biasing stores exponents as unsigned values; restoring is a division method.

qs.stem: According to IEEE standard 754, how many bits are allotted to mantissa for double-precision representation of real numbers?
qs.sol: IEEE 754 double-precision format allocates 64 bits total: 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits, and 52 mantissa bits. The mantissa stores the significant digits of the number after normalization, providing precision for real number representation.
qs.rel: Double precision: 52-bit fraction, 11-bit exponent (bias 1023), 1 sign, total 64 bits. Single: 23-bit fraction. Extended precision: 80 bits. Hidden leading 1 gives effectively 53 bits of precision.

qs.stem: Which of the following specifies the micro-operation to be executed by a Control Unit?
qs.sol:
A control word contains the control bits that select the micro-operations performed by the control unit.

Its fields activate the required control signals in a microprogrammed design.
qs.rel: A control word is the set of control bits selecting micro-operations in a cycle. A microinstruction contains a control word plus sequencing info. Control memory holds the microprogram.

qs.stem: Which of the following data transfer modes between CPU and I/O devices has the data transfer initiated by the instruction of a computer program executed by the CPU?
qs.sol: Programmed I/O is the correct mode because it requires the CPU to execute specific instructions to manage data transfer directly. In contrast, Interrupt-driven I/O relies on hardware signals to initiate transfers, while DMA uses a dedicated controller that bypasses the CPU for data movement.
qs.rel: Programmed I/O transfers are initiated by instructions in the program executed by CPU. Interrupt-initiated transfers start when the device signals; DMA starts under DMA controller control.

qs.stem: By how many different ways micro-operations encountered in digital computers are classified?
qs.sol:
Micro-operations in digital computers are classified into four categories.

The Four Types

Register Transfer Micro-operations

Arithmetic Micro-operations

Logic Micro-operations

Shift Micro-operations
qs.rel: Micro-operation categories: register transfer, arithmetic, logic, shift. Each is an elementary operation on register contents performed in one clock pulse. Micro-op notation such as R2 <- R1.

qs.stem: A floating point number is said to be normalised if:

opts.A: The most significant digit of the mantissa is zero
opts.B: The least significant digit of the mantissa is zero
opts.C: The least significant digit of the mantissa is non-zero
opts.D: The most significant digit of the mantissa is non-zero

qs.sol:
A normalised mantissa has a nonzero most significant digit.

Otherwise the radix point can be shifted and the exponent adjusted to obtain a normalised form.
qs.rel: Normalised form requires a non-zero leading mantissa digit (1.xxx in binary). Otherwise the radix point can be shifted, giving multiple representations. Normalisation maximises precision.

qs.stem: In which of the following addressing modes is the content of an index register added to the address part of the instruction to obtain an effective address?
qs.sol:
Indexed addressing computes the effective address by adding the index-register contents to the instruction’s address field.

Thus EA = address field + index register.
qs.rel: Indexed mode: EA = index register + address part, ideal for arrays. Base-register mode adds a base register (relocation); relative adds PC; indirect uses memory pointer.

qs.stem: A memory module with a printed circuit board on which DRAM chips are mounted on both sides is called:
qs.sol:
A DIMM is a dual inline memory module with DRAM chips on a circuit board.

Its two sides have separate electrical contacts.
qs.rel: DIMM: dual inline memory module with DRAM chips on a PCB, separate contacts on both sides. SIMM has contacts mirrored on both sides. SO-DIMM is for laptops. DDR generations changed pin counts.

qs.stem: How will (0.10101)2 be represented using normalised scientific notation?
qs.sol: To normalize the binary number (0.10101)₂, we must express it in the form 1.xxxx × 2ⁿ. Currently, the binary point is before the first non-zero digit. Shifting it one position to the right gives 1.0101. To maintain equality, we multiply by 2⁻¹. Thus, the normalized form is 1.0101 × 2⁻¹.
qs.rel: Normalising (0.10101)2: shift the point one place right to get 1.0101 x 2^-1. Fractions below 1 get negative exponents; binary to scientific notation needs leading 1.

qs.stem:
What is the meaning of this arithmetic micro-operation?
 R3 ← R1 + R̅2 + 1

opts.A: Content of R1 plus R2 transferred to R3
opts.B: Content of R1 plus the 2’s complement of R2 transferred to R3
opts.C: Content of R1 plus the 1’s complement of R2 transferred to R3
opts.D: Content of R1 plus R2 after increments transferred to R3

qs.sol:
The given micro-operation is: R3 ← R1 + R̅2 + 1.

Step 1: R̅2 represents the 1’s complement of R2. This means each bit of R2 is inverted (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0).

Step 2: Adding 1 to the 1’s complement of R2 gives the 2’s complement of R2. This is a standard method to represent negative numbers in binary arithmetic.

Step 3: Therefore, R3 gets the sum of R1 and the 2’s complement of R2. This operation effectively performs R1 - R2 in binary arithmetic. …
qs.rel: R3 <- R1 + R2' + 1 where R2' is the 1's complement: adding 1 forms the 2's complement, so the operation is subtraction R1 - R2. Other arithmetic micro-ops: increment, decrement, add with carry.

qs.stem:
The 4-bit registers R1 and R2 initially have the following values.
 R1 : 1010
 R2 : 1100
 What is the content of R1 and R2 after execution of this micro-operation?
 R1 ← R1 ⊕ R2
 ⊕ is a symbol of Ex-OR.
qs.sol:
Step 1: Perform Ex-OR operation between R1 (1010) and R2 (1100).

Step 2: Bit-by-bit Ex-OR: 1⊕1=0, 0⊕1=1, 1⊕0=1, 0⊕0=0.

Step 3: Result is 0110, which updates R1.

Step 4: R2 remains unchanged as 1100.
qs.rel: Bitwise XOR: 1010 xor 1100 = 0110 (equal bits give 0). AND gives 1000, OR gives 1110, complement of R1 is 0101. XOR with itself clears a register.

qs.stem: Which of the following floating point numbers is represented by the 0 1000 0011 1001 0100 0000 0000 0000 000 in IEEE 754 standard?
qs.sol: First, parse the 32-bit binary string into IEEE 754 single precision components. The sign bit is 0, indicating a positive number. The exponent bits are 1000 0011, which equals 131 in decimal. Subtracting the bias of 127 gives an actual exponent of 4. The mantissa bits represent a fraction that combines with the implicit leading one to form 1.578125. Finally, multiply this significand by 2 to the power of 4 to get the final value of 25.25.
qs.rel: IEEE 754 decoding: split sign, exponent, fraction; subtract bias 127; restore hidden 1. 0 10000011 1001010... gives 1.100101 x 2^4 = 25.25. Hex form is 41CA0000.

qs.stem: If the value of multiplicand is 10111 and multiplier is 10011, what will be the result produced by Booth’s multiplication algorithm in decimal?
qs.sol:
Booth's method treats these five-bit operands as signed two's-complement values: 10111 is −9 and 10011 is −13.

Their product is 117.
qs.rel: Booth's algorithm multiplies signed 2's complement numbers: 00/11 shift, 01 add multiplicand, 10 subtract multiplicand, then arithmetic shift right. Here -9 x -13 = 117. Booth reduces additions for runs of 1s.

qs.stem:
The 8-bit register A and B initially have the following values:
 A = 01110110
 B = 10000101
 What is the 8-bit value in each register after execution of the following micro-operation?
 A ← A + B
 B ← B + 1
qs.sol:
Step 1: Perform binary addition of A and B: 01110110 + 10000101.

Step 2: Add bit by bit from right to left, including carry.

Step 3: The sum is 11111011 with a carry-out of 1, which is discarded in 8-bit arithmetic.

Step 4: Increment B by 1: 10000101 + 1 = 10000110.

Final values: A = 11111011, B = 10000110.
qs.rel: Register micro-operations: A <- A + B is binary addition with carry-out discarded in 8 bits; B <- B + 1 increments. Check overflow by sign bits and carry rules. Increment is an arithmetic micro-op.

qs.stem: What is Booth’s algorithm used for?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Booth’s algorithm multiplies signed binary integers.

Recoding runs of multiplier bits reduces some partial products.

It is a multiplication technique rather than base conversion.

qs.stem: How many bits are used in the exponent part of IEEE single precision for the representation of floating point numbers?
qs.sol:
Concept

A binary floating-point word stores a sign, a biased exponent, and a fraction in separate fields. Their stored widths add to the word width; the implicit leading significand bit is not stored in the fraction field.

Application

IEEE binary32 uses a 32-bit stored word.

Its sign field uses 1 bit and its stored fraction field uses 23 bits.

Subtract the other fields from the word width: 32 − 1 − 23 = 8 bits for the exponent field.

Cross-check

The field widths add back to 32: 1 + 8 + 23 = 32. Thus the exponent part uses 8 bits.

qs.stem: In the RTL notation R2(0-7), the expression (0-7) denotes:

opts.A: A control signal associated with R2
opts.D:
A portion of register R2 consisting of bits 0 through 7

E

Question not attempted

qs.sol: In register-transfer notation, R2 denotes one register and the parenthesized range identifies its bit positions. R2(0–7) means the portion containing bits 0 through 7 of that register. It does not name eight separate registers or memory addresses.

The operation executed on data stored in registers is called a micro operation.
 Micro operations are the functional or atomic operations of a processor.
 These are low-level instructions that are used in some designs to implement complex machine instructions.
IEEE 754 defines exponent sizes as 8 bits for single precision (32-bit), 11 bits for double precision (64-bit), and 15 bits for quadruple precision (128-bit).

qs.stem: In single-precision, double-precision and extended-precision representation of floating point numbers, as defined by ANSI/IEEE standard 754-1985, the no. of bits used are ____ respectively.
qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: the printed “extended-precision” term does not identify an implementation. This answer interprets it as the x87 double-extended format. Single precision uses 32 bits, double precision uses 64 bits, and x87 extended precision uses 80 bits. Other extended implementations can use a different storage width, so the printed wording alone does not establish a unique final width.

qs.stem: If the multiplier Q is 1101 (-3 in decimal) and 4 bit registers are in use, then in Booth's technique for multiplication the number of addition and subtractions required are:
qs.sol:
For Q = 1101 and initial Q−1 = 0, examine adjacent Booth pairs from LSB to MSB: (Q0,Q−1)=10, (Q1,Q0)=01, (Q2,Q1)=10, (Q3,Q2)=11. The operations are subtraction, addition, subtraction and no operation. Therefore Booth's technique requires 1 addition and 2 subtractions.

The provisional key marked '1 addition and 1 subtraction'; Booth recoding of the multiplier bit pairs 10, 01, 10, 11 gives subtract, add, subtract, so the answer is 1 addition and 2 subtractions.

qs.stem: An arithmetic right shift is performed on the 8-bit 2's complement number 11100100. The result is:
qs.sol: An arithmetic right shift preserves the sign bit of a two’s-complement value. For 11100100, copy the leading 1 into the new most-significant bit and move every remaining bit one place right, discarding the old last bit. The result is 11110010.

qs.stem: Let A = 1111 1010 and B = 0000 1010 be two 8-bit 2's complement numbers. What will their product in 2's complement be?
qs.sol: First, convert the binary numbers to decimal. A = 1111 1010 is negative (MSB=1). Invert bits to get 0000 0101, add 1 to get 0000 0110 (6), so A = -6. B = 0000 1010 is positive, equal to 10. Multiply: -6 × 10 = -60. Convert -60 back to 8-bit 2's complement: Binary of 60 is 0011 1100. Invert to get 1100 0011, add 1 to get 1100 0100.

Modified from the official paper: replaced the invalid final binary digit 2 with 0 and changed the preceding 0 to 1, giving 1111 0110. In eight-bit two’s complement, this is −10. Adding 0000 0101 (+5) gives 1111 1011, or −5.

topics.deep:
- **Signed number representations (n bits):**

| Scheme | Range | Zero | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sign-magnitude | -(2^(n-1)-1) to +(2^(n-1)-1) | two zeros | MSB sign: **0 = positive, 1 = negative** |
| 1's complement | same as above | two zeros | invert all bits |
| **2's complement** | **-2^(n-1) to +2^(n-1)-1** | one zero | invert + 1; used in practice |

- 8-bit 2's complement: -128 to +127. Subtraction R1 - R2 = R1 + (2's complement of R2). **Overflow** (signed add) occurs when two operands of the same sign give a result of opposite sign; carry-out alone does not signal signed overflow. A final carry in unsigned addition means the result exceeded the bit width, and in 8-bit register arithmetic the carry-out is simply discarded.
- **Adders:** half adder (S = A xor B, C = A.B), full adder (S = A xor B xor Cin), ripple-carry (slow), carry-look-ahead (fast).
- **IEEE 754 formats:**

| Format | Total | Sign | Exponent (bias) | Fraction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single | 32 | 1 | **8 (127)** | **23** |
| Double | 64 | 1 | **11 (1023)** | **52** |

- Value = (-1)^s x 1.f x 2^(e - bias); the leading 1 is implicit ("hidden bit"). Special cases: e = 0, f = 0 gives **zero**; e all 1s, f = 0 gives **infinity**; e all 1s, f nonzero gives **NaN**; e = 0, f nonzero gives denormalised number. Single precision about 7 decimal digits, range about 3.4 x 10^38; double about 15-16 digits.
- **Worked conversion to IEEE (single):** 25.25 = 11001.01 = 1.100101 x 2^4. Exponent = 4 + 127 = 131 = 10000011. Fraction = 100101 followed by zeros. Word = 0 10000011 10010100000000000000000 = **41CA0000** hex. Second example: -5.75 = -101.11 = -1.0111 x 2^2; exponent 129 = 10000001; sign 1; word = 1 10000001 01110000... = **C0B80000**.
- **Worked decode:** 0 10000011 1001010... -> e = 131 - 127 = 4; mantissa 1.100101 -> shift 4 places = 11001.01 = 25.25.
- **Normalisation:** shift the mantissa until its most significant digit is non-zero (binary form 1.xxx), adjusting the exponent. Example: (0.10101)2 = 1.0101 x 2^-1. Floating add/subtract steps: **align exponents** (shift smaller number right), add/subtract mantissas, **normalise**, round, check overflow/underflow. Multiplication: add exponents (remove extra bias), multiply mantissas, normalise.
- **Booth's multiplication** (signed 2's complement multiplier recoding): registers A (accumulator), Q (multiplier), Q-1 (extra bit), M (multiplicand), count n. Examine Q0 Q-1: **00 or 11 -> only arithmetic shift right**; **01 -> A = A + M then shift**; **10 -> A = A - M then shift**. Worked: M = 0011 (3), Q = 1110 (-2). Start A=0000, Q=1110, Q-1=0. Step 1 (00): shift -> 0000 0111 0. Step 2 (10): A = 0000 + 1101 = 1101, shift -> 1110 1011 1. Step 3 (11): shift -> 1111 0101 1. Step 4 (11): shift -> 1111 1010 1. Result AQ = 11111010 = **-6**. Check by hand: operand 10111 = -9 and 10011 = -13 give +117.
- **Division:** restoring (add divisor back if remainder negative) vs non-restoring. Multiplication of n x n bits gives 2n-bit product.
- **Micro-operations** = elementary operations on data in registers. **Four classes:** **register transfer** (R2 <- R1), **arithmetic** (add, subtract, increment, decrement), **logic** (AND, OR, XOR, complement), **shift** (logical, circular, arithmetic). The **control unit** issues micro-operations via a **control word**.
- **Arithmetic micro-ops:** R3 <- R1 + R2 (add); R3 <- R1 + R2' + 1 (**R1 plus 2's complement of R2 = R1 - R2**; R2' is the 1's complement); R1 <- R1 + 1 (increment); R1 <- R1 - 1.
- **Logic micro-ops on R1 = 1010, R2 = 1100:** AND = 1000; OR = 1110; XOR = 0110; NOT R1 = 0101. **Shifts of 1010:** logical shift left 0100; logical shift right 0101; arithmetic shift right 1101 (sign copied); circular left 0101. Bit-wise worked add: A = 01110110 + B = 10000101 = 11111011 with carry-out 1 discarded.
- **Datapath components:** ALU is a combinational circuit performing arithmetic, logic and shift; status flags (carry, zero, sign, overflow) are set by results. Registers connect through a common bus with multiplexers.
- **Misfiled PYQs in this topic (revise with other topics):** address-count of an instruction (ADD R1,A,B = 3 address; PUSH = 0 address), programmed I/O (CPU polls, initiated by program instruction), indexed mode (EA = index register + address part), DIMM (dual inline memory module, DRAM chips on both sides), supercomputer speed in FLOPS, sign bit definition.
- **Likely question angles:** (1) represent a decimal number in IEEE 754 single or decode a hex word; (2) bias value and field widths for double precision; (3) range of n-bit 2's complement; (4) negative number in 2's complement (-5 in 8 bits = 11111011); (5) detect overflow in signed addition; (6) Booth recoding rules for a given Qn Qn+1; (7) result of logic micro-operation such as AND/OR/complement; (8) arithmetic vs logical shift result; (9) identify the zero/infinity/NaN encodings; (10) steps of floating-point addition.

topics.title: 7. Multimedia, Image/Audio Formats & MS Office
topics.theory:
- **Image formats:** **JPEG = Joint Photographic Experts Group** (lossy, photos); **GIF = Graphics Interchange Format** (**256 colours, 8-bit palette**, supports animation & 1-bit transparency); PNG (lossless, alpha); BMP/**.DIB = Device Independent Bitmap**; WMF/EMF = Windows (Enhanced) Metafile (vector); **WAV is audio, not an image format**. **Colour depth:** 8 bpp = 256 colours = **palette images**; **16 bpp = high colour**; 24 bpp = true colour.
- **Audio/video:** **MPEG audio = .mp3 (MPEG-1 Layer 3)**; MPEG-4 = .mp4; MPEG macroblock = **16×16 pixels**; **MIDI = Musical Instrument Digital Interface**; **digitisation uses sampling and quantisation**; **data compression** reduces file size. **Haptic technology** = **tactile** (touch) feedback.
- **Authoring tools:** **PowerPoint = card/slide-based** (as per exam key); **Flash/Director = time-based**; Authorware/IconAuthor = **icon-based** (flowline); **HyperCard = card-based, created for Mac**; **Lingo = scripting language of Macromedia/Adobe Director**. **Flash keyframes:** **F6 = insert keyframe, F5 = insert frame, F7 = blank keyframe; Shift+F6 = delete keyframe/clear**; a keyframe holds a change.
- **MS Word shortcuts:** **Ctrl+Z undo**, Ctrl+Y redo, **Ctrl+R right-align**, **Ctrl+J justify**, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+L left, **Ctrl+T hanging indent**, **Ctrl+H find & replace**, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+Enter page break, **Ctrl+] increase font by 1 pt**, Ctrl+[ decrease. **Excel:** workbook = file (contains sheets); **Ctrl+G / F5 = Go To**. **PowerPoint:** background for all slides is set in the **Slide Master**; enhances presentations with pictures, charts, sound, video, animation.

qs.stem: _____ is used to reduce the size of multimedia files.
qs.sol: Data compression reduces the size of multimedia files by encoding data more efficiently.
qs.rel: Compression reduces storage and bandwidth: lossless (ZIP, PNG, GIF, FLAC) vs lossy (JPEG, MP3, MPEG). Techniques: RLE, Huffman, LZW, DCT-based coding. Compression ratio = original size / compressed size.

qs.stem: In JPEG image format, what is the full form of JPEG?
qs.sol: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group, the group associated with the image-compression standard.
qs.rel: JPEG = Joint Photographic Experts Group: lossy compression for photographs, 24-bit colour, no transparency. Neighbours: GIF (256 colours, animation), PNG (lossless, alpha), MPEG (Moving Picture Experts Group).

qs.stem: JPEG (image compression standard) stands for ____________.
qs.sol: JPEG is the abbreviation for Joint Photographic Experts Group, which developed the image-compression standard.
qs.rel: JPEG is a lossy standard using DCT, quantisation and entropy coding; quality versus file size trade-off. JPEG 2000 uses wavelets. Repeated saving degrades quality.

qs.stem: What is the full form of JPEG image forms?
qs.sol: JPEG expands to Joint Photographic Experts Group, the name of the standards committee.
qs.rel: JPEG named after the Joint Photographic Experts Group committee; extension .jpg/.jpeg. Related full forms: MPEG, MIDI, GIF, PNG (Portable Network Graphics), TIFF (Tagged Image File Format).

qs.stem: Which of the following is not the file formats of graphics?
qs.sol:
A graphics file format is a file format used to store image data - pixel colour values (raster) or path/shape data (vector) - so that visual content can be displayed or edited.

Checking each option against this definition: GIF, JPG, and PNG are all raster image file formats that store picture data, so all three qualify as graphics formats. WAV instead stores digitized sound-wave samples (PCM audio data) - it carries no pixel information at all, so it is not a graphics format.

GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) - stores raster images and simple animations using LZW compression.

JPG (JPEG) - a compressed raster format used for photographs. …
qs.rel: Graphics formats: GIF, JPG, PNG, BMP, TIFF, SVG. WAV is an audio format. Know audio (WAV, MP3, MIDI), video (AVI, MP4, MOV, MPG) and image families.

qs.stem: With respect to image types, JPEG stands for ____.
qs.sol: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group.
qs.rel: JPEG expansion check: Joint Photographic Experts Group. Other multimedia standards committees: MPEG (Moving Picture Experts Group), JBIG (bi-level images).

qs.stem:
Which principles are used in digitization of multimedia content?
 I. Sampling
 II. Quantization
qs.sol: Digitization of multimedia content uses sampling and quantization.
qs.rel: Digitisation = sampling (time discretisation) + quantisation (amplitude discretisation) + encoding. Nyquist: sample at least twice the highest frequency. CD audio: 44.1 kHz, 16-bit.

qs.stem: Images known as "high color images" consist of _____ color depths.
qs.sol: High color images commonly use 16 bits per pixel.
qs.rel: Colour depth: 8-bit = 256 colours (palette), 16-bit = high colour (65,536), 24-bit = true colour (16.7 million). More bits per pixel means larger files.

qs.stem: How many colours are supported by GIF images?
qs.sol: GIF images use an 8-bit palette, so they can support up to 256 colours.
qs.rel: GIF supports 256 colours (8-bit palette), LZW lossless compression, animation and single-colour transparency. For photographs use JPEG; for lossless with alpha use PNG.

qs.stem: What is the extension of MPEG Audio file?
qs.sol:
MPEG defines a family of multimedia compression standards spanning both video and audio. Within it, MPEG Audio Layer III (universally known as "MP3") is the specific scheme for compressed digital audio, and such compressed MPEG audio files are conventionally saved with the .mp3 extension — distinct from the container formats used for MPEG video.

This question asks specifically for the extension of an MPEG AUDIO file (not a full MPEG video stream). MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III audio files are universally saved and recognized with the .mp3 extension, so .mp3 is the correct choice here. …
qs.rel: MPEG audio file extension is .mp3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer III). MPEG-4 video is .mp4. .mov is Apple QuickTime. MPEG layers I, II, III give increasing compression.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about GIF format?

opts.A: GIF stands for Graphics Interchange Format.
opts.C: It is used for vector image files.

qs.sol: GIF stands for Graphics Interchange Format. It is a raster image format that commonly supports a limited 256-colour palette.
qs.rel: GIF = Graphics Interchange Format: raster, 256 colours, lossless LZW, supports animation. Not vector, not lossy. Vector formats include SVG, WMF, EMF.

qs.stem: In MPEG layered bitstream structure, macroblock layer consists of _____ pixels?
qs.sol: In MPEG video coding, a macroblock commonly consists of a 16 x 16 block of pixels.
qs.rel: MPEG hierarchy: sequence, group of pictures, picture, slice, macroblock (16 x 16 pixels), block (8 x 8). Frame types: I (intra), P (predicted), B (bidirectional).

qs.stem: Haptic technology is used to provide ______ feedback to a user.
qs.sol: Haptic technology simulates the sense of touch by applying forces, vibrations, or motions to a user. This tactile feedback enables interaction with digital devices through physical sensations rather than just visual or auditory cues alone.
qs.rel: Haptic technology gives tactile (touch) feedback via vibration or force, used in games, phones and VR gloves. Auditory = sound; olfactory = smell; visual = display.

qs.stem: MIDI stands for ____?
qs.sol: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface.
qs.rel: MIDI = Musical Instrument Digital Interface: transmits note events (not sampled audio) between instruments and computers, so files are tiny. WAV stores samples, MP3 compresses them.

qs.stem: Which of the following image type has an extension as .dib?
qs.sol: The .dib extension stands for Device Independent Bitmap, which is a bitmap image type.
qs.rel: DIB = Device Independent Bitmap, a bitmap image type (like .bmp). WMF/EMF are Windows metafiles (vector + bitmap). RLE is a run-length encoded bitmap form.

qs.stem: Images with colors depths of eight bits have 256 colors and it is known as _____.
qs.sol: An 8-bit colour-depth image can represent 256 colours using a colour palette, so it is known as a palette image.
qs.rel: 8-bit colour depth gives 256 colours, called palette (indexed) images. 16-bit high colour; 24-bit true colour; 1-bit monochrome.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about Lingo?

opts.B: It is used in Macromedia Director.
opts.C: It was developed by John Henry Thompson and Erik Neumann.
opts.D: It is a multimedia authoring tool for Windows platform.

qs.sol:
Concept: A programming/scripting language and an authoring tool (application) are distinct layers. A scripting language is code that runs inside a host application to control its behaviour; an authoring tool is the standalone software product used to build and package the final project. A statement about a scripting language is incorrect if it instead describes the host application.

Application: Lingo is the scripting language built into Macromedia (now Adobe) Director, used to add interactivity and control behaviour inside Director movies. It was created primarily by John Henry Thompson, with later versions of the language developed further by Erik Neumann. …
qs.rel: Lingo is Director's scripting language (created by John Henry Thompson), not itself an authoring tool. Director is time-based using Score, Stage and Cast. Flash uses ActionScript.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a time-based multimedia authoring tool?
qs.sol: Macromedia Flash is a time-based multimedia authoring tool because animation and content are organized along a timeline.
qs.rel: Time-based authoring uses a timeline: Flash and Director. Icon-based: Authorware, IconAuthor. Card/page-based: HyperCard, ToolBook. Choose by organising metaphor.

qs.stem: PowerPoint is a __________ multimedia authoring tool that runs on Windows environment.
qs.sol: PowerPoint organizes content as slides/cards, so it is classified as a card-based multimedia authoring tool.
qs.rel: Authoring tool classification: card/slide-based (PowerPoint per key, HyperCard, ToolBook), icon-based (Authorware), time-based (Flash, Director). PowerPoint runs on Windows and Mac.

qs.stem: Which of the following multimedia authoring tools is created for Mac operating system?
qs.sol: HyperCard was created for the Mac operating system. It is a classic card-based multimedia authoring tool.
qs.rel: HyperCard was developed by Apple for the Macintosh, card-based with HyperTalk scripting. ToolBook is Windows page-based; IconAuthor is icon-based.

qs.stem: Which statement is correct about Keyframes in Flash?

opts.A: It is a copy of the previous regular frame.
opts.B: Ctrl + F5 shortcut key is used to insert a duplicate Keyframe.
opts.C: Shift + F5 shortcut key is used to delete Keyframes.
opts.D: F7 shortcut key is used to insert a blank Keyframe.

qs.sol: In Flash, F7 is the shortcut used to insert a blank keyframe. The other listed shortcuts/statements do not describe this action correctly.
qs.rel: Flash keyframes mark where content changes; F6 inserts a keyframe, F7 a blank keyframe, F5 a frame. Shift+F6 clears a keyframe, Shift+F5 removes a frame. A keyframe is not just a copy of the previous frame.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statements is/are true about Keyframes in Flash?

(i) A Flash project contains only one Keyframe. 
(ii) Ctrl + F5 shortcut key is used to insert a duplicate Keyframe.
qs.sol: A Flash project can contain many keyframes, so statement (i) is false. Ctrl + F5 is not the shortcut for inserting a duplicate keyframe, so statement (ii) is also false.
qs.rel: A Flash movie normally has many keyframes along the timeline; frames between are tweened. Keyframe shortcut is F6, Ctrl+F5 is not a keyframe command. Layers hold separate animations.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about icon-based multimedia authoring tool?

opts.A: In this type of authoring tools, each icon is used for a specific task.
opts.B: In this type of authoring tool, the elements are organised as pages of a book or a stack of cards.
opts.C: PowerPoint is an icon-based multimedia authoring tool.
opts.D: The Authorware icon-based multimedia authoring tools runs only on Windows platform.

qs.sol: In icon-based multimedia authoring tools, each icon represents or performs a specific task in the authoring flow.
qs.rel: Icon-based authoring: each icon performs a task (display, interaction, calculation) arranged in a flowline, e.g. Authorware. Time-based tools organise by timeline; card-based by cards linked together.

qs.stem: Which shortcut key is used to insert frame in Flash?
qs.sol: In Adobe Flash, pressing the F5 key is the standard shortcut to insert a frame on the timeline. This action extends the duration of the current layer or keyframe.
qs.rel: In Flash F5 inserts a frame, F6 keyframe, F7 blank keyframe. Frames extend duration; keyframes define content change. Shift+F5 removes frame.

qs.stem: What is the function of “Shift + F6” shortcut key in Flash?
qs.sol: The shortcut Shift + F6 in Adobe Flash deletes the currently selected keyframe on the timeline. This distinguishes it from other shortcuts that insert new frames or create blank keyframes instead of removing existing ones.
qs.rel: Shift+F6 clears (deletes) a keyframe in Flash. Shift+F5 removes a frame. F6 inserts keyframe, F7 blank keyframe. Convert to symbol is F8.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a shortcut key to undo last action in MS Word?
qs.sol: Ctrl+Z is a shortcut key to undo last action in MS Word
qs.rel: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo (or F4 repeat). Related: Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+B/I/U bold, italic, underline.

qs.stem: What is the shortcut key for right alignment of the paragraph in a Microsoft Word document?
qs.sol:
shortcut key for right alignment of the paragraph in a Microsoft Word document is 

Ctrl + R
qs.rel: Alignment keys in Word: Ctrl+L left, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+R right, Ctrl+J justify. Indent keys: Ctrl+M indent, Ctrl+T hanging indent.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a shortcut key to justify paragraph alignment in MS-Word?
qs.sol: Ctrl + J is a shortcut key to justify paragraph alignment in MS-Word.
qs.rel: Ctrl+J justifies; Ctrl+I is italics, Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Y redoes. Justify aligns both left and right margins by adjusting spaces.

qs.stem: What is the function of Ctrl + T in MS Word?
qs.sol: Hanging indent
qs.rel: Ctrl+T creates a hanging indent (first line outdented, rest indented); Ctrl+M increases left indent; Ctrl+Shift+T reduces hanging indent. Used in bibliographies.

qs.stem: Which is the shortcut key to Find and Replace action in MS-Word?
qs.sol: Ctrl + H is used for Find and Replace
qs.rel: Ctrl+H opens Find and Replace; Ctrl+F opens Find (navigation pane); Ctrl+G opens Go To. In Excel Ctrl+H also replaces.

qs.stem: Which key open a Goto window in Microsoft Excel?
qs.sol: Ctrl + G is the key that open a Goto window in Microsoft Excel
qs.rel: Ctrl+G or F5 opens Go To in Excel. Related: F2 edit cell, F4 absolute reference, Ctrl+Home goes to A1, Ctrl+Arrow jumps to data edge, Ctrl+Shift+L filter.

qs.stem: Each Microsoft Excel file is also known as _____.
qs.sol:
When you open Excel, the whole file you save (like marks.xlsx) is called a Workbook.

Inside a workbook, there are multiple Worksheets (Sheet1, Sheet2, etc.).

A worksheet contains rows and columns (cells).

So remember:

File = Workbook

Page inside file = Worksheet
qs.rel: Excel file = workbook, containing worksheets (tabs), each made of rows and columns of cells. Word file is a document; PowerPoint file is a presentation of slides.

qs.stem: In Microsoft PowerPoint, background image can be added for all the slides by editing which slide?
qs.sol: Slide Master
qs.rel: Slide Master controls background, fonts and layout for all slides in a PowerPoint presentation (View > Slide Master). Layouts and themes inherit from it.

qs.stem:
Microsoft PowerPoint helps to enhance our presentation with _____.
 Statements:
 I. Pictures and charts
 II. Sound effect
 III. Tables
qs.sol: I, II and III
qs.rel: PowerPoint can embed pictures, charts, tables, sound, video, animation, SmartArt, hyperlinks. Transitions affect slide change; animations affect objects on a slide.

qs.stem: Which of the following is the way to break a page in Microsoft Word?

opts.B: Double Clicking at the end of the page
opts.D: Double Clicking at the beginning of the page

qs.sol: Pressing “Ctrl + Enter”
qs.rel: Ctrl+Enter inserts a manual page break in Word; Ctrl+Shift+Enter inserts column break. Page Down scrolls only. Insert > Page Break is the menu path.

qs.stem: The selected text’s font in Microsoft Word document will ______ on pressing “Ctrl + ]” keys.
qs.sol:
When you press Ctrl + ] in Microsoft Word, the font size of the selected text increases by 1 point.

This is a standard keyboard shortcut for increasing font size incrementally.

The shortcut does not decrease the font size or change it by more than 1 point.
qs.rel: Ctrl+] grows selected text by 1 pt; Ctrl+[ shrinks by 1 pt. Ctrl+Shift+> and < step through the preset font sizes. Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog.

qs.stem: Excel workbook is a collection of :
qs.sol: A workbook is the Excel file that contains one or more worksheets. Charts can be objects or chart sheets within it, but they do not define the workbook.

.mp3 is a widely used audio file format used for music and sound.

.gif is an image/animation format.

.jpeg is an image format.

.docx is a document format (MS Word).

Hence, the only audio extension among the options is .mp3.

qs.stem: Which of the following keyboard shortcut combinations is commonly used to perform the “Select All” operation in Microsoft Windows ?
qs.sol:
Recall the standard Windows editing shortcuts.

X, C and V act on a selection or clipboard content.

A with Ctrl selects all content in the active context.

Answer: .xlsx

.xlsx is the file extension used for Excel workbook files created by Excel 2007 and later. It uses the Office Open XML format.

Modern Excel workbooks: .xlsx (Excel 2007+)

Older Excel workbooks: .xls (used before Excel 2007)

The other choices ('xcl', 'xelx', and 'excel') are not valid Excel file extensions; 'excel' is the program name, not a file extension.

qs.stem: Which one is the default file extension of the latest versions of MS Excel spreadsheets ?
qs.sol: Modern Excel workbooks use the Office Open XML workbook format; its standard filename extension is .xlsx. The other suffixes do not name Excel’s default workbook format.

qs.stem: Which of the following file extensions is commonly used for storing audio files?
qs.sol: The WAV format stores digitized waveform audio. The other listed extensions represent images or documents.

qs.stem: Which of the following file extensions is commonly used for storing audio files?
qs.sol: WAV is a waveform-audio container used for sound data.

qs.stem: Which of the following shortcut of Keyboard will help to select the entire text in the document ?
qs.sol: The standard Select All shortcut in a document is Ctrl+A. Copy, paste, and cut act on an existing selection; they do not select the entire document.

qs.stem: The shortcut key to ‘Find and Replace’ option in Windows is :
qs.sol: The conventional shortcut for Replace is Ctrl + H. The other shortcuts perform Cut, Copy and Paste respectively.

qs.stem: You can use ………. to copy selected text and ………. to paste it into a document.
qs.sol: The standard shortcuts are Ctrl+C to copy and Ctrl+V to paste. Ctrl+P prints and Ctrl+S saves; the Shift/Alt pair is not the standard copy/paste pair.
JPEG expands to Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee associated with the well-known image-compression standard. “Photographic” and “Experts Group” are the defining words in its full form.

In Microsoft Word, the standard shortcut key used to open the  Print  dialog box is  Ctrl + P .
 It is a universal print command across most software applications.

qs.stem: The file extension .docx is the default extension for which type of file ?
qs.sol:
An extension identifies the usual file format associated with an application.

The Office Open XML document format produced by Microsoft Word uses .docx.

Thus the extension belongs to a Word document.

qs.stem: Which of the following file extensions is generally not used for storing video files ?
qs.sol:
AVI, FLV and MP4 are video container formats.

PDF is a document format and is generally used for pages of text and graphics, not video storage.

qs.stem: In MS Word 2019, which keyboard shortcut applies italic formatting to selected text ?
qs.sol: “Optic Fiber Cable” is the expansion marked in the printed source and denotes the physical medium for optical data transmission. “Optical Fiber Communication” describes the transmission process, so it does not expand the cable term used here.

qs.stem: In MS Word 2019, which keyboard shortcut applies italic formatting to selected text ?

opts.D:
Alt + I

E

Question not attempted

qs.sol:
In Word, Ctrl+I toggles italic formatting for the selected text.

The same command can remove italics when already applied.
Animation creates the illusion of movement by displaying a sequence of drawings or images with small changes between frames. The described simulated movement of drawn objects is therefore animation.
Excel is spreadsheet software used for tabular data, formulas, and calculations.
Answer:  Landscape

qs.stem: In MS-Excel, to remove extra spaces from a text except single space between words, we can use ……….. function.
qs.sol: Excel TRIM removes leading and trailing spaces and reduces repeated internal spaces to one. It preserves a single separator between words.

qs.stem: Which of the following software would you prefer most to write a formal application?
qs.sol:
Answer:  Microsoft Word is the best choice for writing a formal application because it is a word processor designed for creating and formatting documents.
 Why Microsoft Word is preferred:
 Offers templates for letters and formal applications.
MS Excel includes built-in functions like SUM(), MIN(), and COUNT(), but there is no direct MULTIPLY() function. Multiplication is performed using the * operator or the PRODUCT() function.

Answer: addition() is not a basic function of MS Excel.
 COUNT() – counts cells that contain numbers (example: =COUNT(A1:A10)).

qs.stem: In the page setup dialog box, following option(s) are available for orientation :
qs.sol:
In page layout and document design (such as in Microsoft Office apps), Orientation refers to the direction in which a document is displayed or printed.

The Page Setup dialog box provides two standard choices:

Portrait: The page is oriented vertically. The height of the page is greater than its width (e.g., standard letters or business reports).

Landscape: The page is rotated 90 degrees and oriented horizontally. The width of the page is greater than its height (e.g., photo albums, wide tables, or presentations).

Since both layout orientations coexist as the primary choices in the Page Setup window, the answer combining Portrait and Landscape is the correct answer.

qs.stem: In the page setup dialog box, following option(s) are available for orientation :
qs.sol:
Answer:  CTRL+V pastes the copied or cut text/object into the document at the cursor location.
 To copy: use Ctrl+C (this leaves the original in place and places a copy on the clipboard).

To cut (move): use Ctrl+X (this removes the original and places it on the clipboard); then use Ctrl+V to paste it elsewhere.

To paste: use Ctrl+V (this inserts the current clipboard contents at the cursor).

Common mistake: Ctrl+V does not copy or cut—it only inserts clipboard contents. Make sure you have copied (Ctrl+C) or cut (Ctrl+X) something first.

Note: Clipboard contents can often be pasted across different applications (for example, from a browser into a document).

Answer:  'cutting the selected text/object / सिलेक्टेड टेक्स्ट/ऑब्जेक्ट को कट करने के लिए' is the correct action for CTRL+X.
 Explanation:  CTRL+X performs a cut operation — it removes the selected content from the document and places it on the clipboard so it can be pasted elsewhere.
 Cut (CTRL+X): removes the selection and stores it on the clipboard.

Copy (CTRL+C): copies the selection to the clipboard without removing it from the document.

Paste (CTRL+V): inserts the clipboard contents at the cursor position.

Why other answer texts are incorrect or less precise:
 The text stating 'pasting the copied text/object' is incorrect because pasting uses CTRL+V, not CTRL+X. …

qs.stem: In MS Excel, the function that returns the largest value in a range A1:A20 is :
qs.sol:

qs.stem: It is acceptable to let long text flow into adjacent cells on a worksheet when —

opts.A: Data will be entered in the adjacent cells
opts.B: No data will be entered in the adjacent cells
opts.C: There is no suitable abbreviation for the text
opts.D:
There is no time to format the text

E

None of these

qs.sol:
Concept: A text entry always belongs to exactly one cell; what changes is how much of it the worksheet draws. A left-aligned text entry that is wider than its own column is rendered across the neighbouring columns, but only while those neighbouring cells are empty. As soon as a neighbouring cell holds a value of its own, the display is clipped at the column border — the full string is still stored and is still shown in the formula bar, but the reader sees only the part that fits.

Applying it here: So letting a long label spill is safe exactly when the cells to its right will stay empty: nothing is hidden and no column has to be widened. …

qs.stem: In the classic menu interface of Microsoft PowerPoint, which menu provides options like Animation Scheme, Custom Animation, and Slide Transition?

opts.D:
Slide Show Menu

E

None of these

qs.sol:
Correct Answer: Slide Show Menu

In the classic Microsoft PowerPoint menu interface, commands such as Animation Scheme, Custom Animation, and Slide Transition are grouped under the Slide Show menu. These commands control how slides and objects appear during a presentation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Slide Show Menu.

qs.stem: In Excel 2016, if you want to insert 3 columns between column G and column H, what should you do?

opts.A: Select column G and right click and select insert for 3 times
opts.B: Select column H and right click and select insert for three times
opts.C: Select column E, F and G and right click and select insert for three times
opts.D: Select column D, E and F and right click and select insert for three times

qs.sol:
Answer: Select column H and right-click and select Insert three times.

In Excel, a new column is inserted to the left of the selected column. To place new columns between G and H, the insertion must happen before column H. Therefore, selecting column H and inserting a column three times creates three new columns between G and H.

qs.stem:
In MS Excel, the following formula is entered in cell D2 :

=IF(AND(B2>=40,C2>=40),IF(B2+C2>=90,"Distinction","Pass"),"Fail")

If the values in cells B2 and C2 are 45 and 42, respectively, what will be the result returned by the formula ?
qs.sol:
Both marks meet the threshold of 40, so the outer IF enters its inner test.

Their sum is 87, below 90, so the inner test returns Pass.

qs.stem: In MS-Office Word, ......... option is used to navigate through structural view of document and ......... option is used to navigate long document through small pictures of each page.
qs.sol:
Step 1: In MS-Office Word, the 'Document Map' option is used to navigate through the structural view of a document by displaying headings and sections. This helps in quickly moving to different parts of the document based on its structure.
 Step 2: The 'Thumbnails' option displays small images of each page, allowing users to navigate through a long document by clicking on the desired page image.
 Step 3: Therefore, the first blank should be filled with 'Document Map' and the second blank with 'Thumbnails'.

topics.deep:
- **Multimedia** = integration of text, graphics, images, audio, video and animation, usually interactive (hypermedia adds links). **Digitisation** needs **sampling** (measuring at regular time intervals) and **quantisation** (rounding to discrete levels). Sampling theorem (Nyquist): sampling rate at least **twice the highest frequency** (CD audio 44.1 kHz, 16 bit). **Data compression** reduces file size: **lossless** (ZIP, PNG, GIF, FLAC; exact recovery; RLE, Huffman, LZW) vs **lossy** (JPEG, MP3, MPEG; discards information).
- **Image size** = width x height x bits per pixel / 8 bytes.
- **Colour depth:** 1 bit = 2 colours (monochrome); 4 bit = 16; **8 bit = 256 colours = palette images**; **16 bit = high colour (65,536)**; **24 bit = true colour (16.7 million)**; 32 bit adds alpha.
- **Image formats:**

| Format | Type | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| **JPEG/JPG** | raster, lossy | **Joint Photographic Experts Group**; photographs; DCT; no transparency |
| **GIF** | raster, lossless (LZW) | **Graphics Interchange Format**; **256 colours (8-bit palette)**; animation; 1-bit transparency |
| PNG | raster, lossless | 24-bit + alpha; web graphics |
| BMP / **DIB** | raster, usually uncompressed | DIB = **Device Independent Bitmap** |
| TIFF | raster | high quality, print/scanning |
| WMF / EMF | vector metafile | Windows Metafile / Enhanced Metafile |
| SVG | vector (XML) | scalable |
| WAV, MP3, MIDI | **audio, not image** | |

- **Audio:** **WAV** uncompressed PCM (Microsoft); **MP3 = MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, extension .mp3** (lossy); AAC, OGG, FLAC (lossless), WMA. **MIDI = Musical Instrument Digital Interface** - stores note/instrument commands not sound samples, tiny files, needs synthesizer.
- **Video:** MPEG-1 (VCD, MP3 audio), MPEG-2 (DVD, broadcast), MPEG-4 (.mp4, H.264, streaming); AVI, MOV, MKV, FLV containers. Frames per second (24, 25, 30). MPEG uses **I, P, B frames**; the picture is divided into **macroblocks of 16 x 16 pixels** (layers: sequence, group of pictures, picture, slice, macroblock, block 8 x 8).
- **Haptic technology** = **tactile (touch) feedback** through vibration/force (game controllers, phones, surgical simulators); olfactory = smell.
- **Authoring tools (by metaphor):** **card/page-based** - HyperCard (**created for Mac**), ToolBook, SuperCard (and PowerPoint as slides/cards per exam key); **icon-based** (flowline of icons, each icon a specific task) - Authorware, IconAuthor; **time-based** (timeline, frames, score) - **Macromedia/Adobe Flash and Director**. **Lingo** = scripting language of Director (a language, not an authoring tool itself). Flash: .fla source, .swf output; ActionScript.
- **Flash timeline shortcuts:**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| F5 | **insert frame** |
| F6 | insert keyframe |
| F7 | insert **blank keyframe** |
| Shift+F5 | remove frame |
| **Shift+F6** | **clear/delete keyframe** |
| F8 | convert to symbol |
| Ctrl+Enter | test movie |

- A **keyframe** marks a change in content/state; a project can contain many; frames between keyframes are tweened (motion, shape). Symbols: graphic, button, movie clip.
- **MS Word shortcuts:**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y | undo / redo |
| Ctrl+B / I / U | bold / italic / underline |
| Ctrl+L / E / R / **J** | left / centre / right / justify |
| **Ctrl+T** | hanging indent (Ctrl+M left indent) |
| **Ctrl+H** | find and replace |
| Ctrl+F / Ctrl+G | find / go to |
| **Ctrl+Enter** | page break (Ctrl+Shift+Enter column break) |
| **Ctrl+]** / Ctrl+[ | increase / decrease font size by 1 pt |
| Ctrl+A / C / X / V | select all / copy / cut / paste |
| Ctrl+S / O / N / P | save / open / new / print |
| F7 | spelling and grammar |
| Shift+F3 | change case |
| Ctrl+K | hyperlink |

- **MS Excel:** a file is a **workbook** containing worksheets; worksheet = rows x columns (1,048,576 x 16,384 in modern versions); cell address like B5; formulas begin with =. Shortcuts: **Ctrl+G or F5 = Go To**, F2 edit cell, F4 absolute reference toggle ($A$1), Alt+= AutoSum, Ctrl+; current date, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+Space (select column), Shift+Space (row), Shift+F11 new sheet. Functions: SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, MIN, IF, VLOOKUP. Extension .xlsx.
- **MS PowerPoint:** presentation of slides; **Slide Master** controls background, fonts, logo for all slides; enhances with pictures, charts, tables, sound, video, animation, transitions. F5 starts slide show from beginning, Shift+F5 from current slide, Ctrl+M new slide, Esc ends show. Extensions .pptx, .ppsx (show).
- **Likely question angles:** (1) lossy vs lossless formats; (2) colours in n-bit depth or file size of an image; (3) which format supports animation/transparency; (4) full forms (MPEG, MIDI, PNG, TIFF, DIB); (5) icon vs card vs time based tools with examples; (6) Flash F-key functions; (7) more Word shortcuts (Ctrl+B/I/U/K/E/L, Ctrl+Shift+...); (8) Excel shortcuts and function results; (9) Slide Master, transitions vs animation in PowerPoint; (10) sampling rate/Nyquist and CD audio specs.
